variants.title: Hamilton · 蓄势／开口／强调
variants.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / stylized-concept.
Asset type: production-oriented main pixel-art DIALOGUE CHARACTER animation study for a Hamilton musical RPG. This must have strong GAME CHARACTER appeal and clear acting, not a neutral historical costume portrait.
REFERENCE IMAGE: the supplied Eliza image is the exact STYLE REFERENCE only. Closely match her sculptural rich pixel shading, deliberately hard stepped pixel contours, dark colored edge outlines, detailed clustered hair, strong silhouette, vivid but controlled material highlights, substantial cloth folds, and attractive slightly animation-stylized proportions. The appearance should belong to the SAME GAME ART SET as this Eliza. Do not copy her gender, dress, book, quill, bowed pose, magenta background or concealed face: the new male character's face is fully visible, expressive and recognizable.
Create ONE WIDE THREE-FRAME SPRITE SHEET: exactly 3 equally sized columns, one complete head-to-upper-thigh portrait per column of the SAME man. Landscape 3:2 image. Strict repeated character design, costume and palette. Every frame has the same scale and registration: hair top, eye line, shoulder baseline, hips baseline and torso x center align across cells. Generous cell gutters, all hair and elbows and extended fingers fully inside each column, no overlap between columns. Deliberately enlarged expression readability without chibi superdeformed proportions or huge anime eyes. Each waist-up character should have a bold, purposeful asymmetrical pose, NEVER both hands politely clasped at waist, NEVER formal portrait standing attention. Strong adult game-character silhouette and physical tension even with closed mouth.
FRAME 1 LEFT: closed-mouth ready/listening state, already in the characteristic acting pose, vivid eyes and brows.
FRAME 2 CENTER: ordinary TALKING frame, preserve body, arms, fingers, costume, hair, skull/eye/ear position EXACTLY as frame 1; change only lips and slight jaw to an obvious small open-mouth vowel with visible dark mouth interior and subtle upper teeth. It must really be an open mouth, not a closed-lip smile.
FRAME 3 RIGHT: EMPHASIZED SPEECH, same rooted body position, eye and head registration; a clearly larger open-mouth stressed syllable and a restrained small increase of the existing hand gesture (about a few centimeters higher/further forward). Energized, not shouting in rage. Avoid changing stance or flipping shoulders.
Pixel craft: nearest-neighbor crisp square pixel structure, complex shading made of hand-placed pixel clusters, purposeful color ramps, slight stylization. Rich detailed sprite like reference Eliza. Do not render a photo, 3D model, smooth illustration, watercolor, a photo pixelation filter, random dither noise or generic static portrait.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha, isolated characters. No checkerboard pattern baked in, no environment, no ground, no shadow behind the figure, no speech bubble, no border, no labels, no text or watermark. If transparency is unavailable use perfectly uniform pure magenta #ff00ff, no pattern. Output exactly three equal-sized frames of ONE character, not three different people. No extra props.
CHARACTER: Alexander Hamilton in the musical's Lin-Manuel Miranda portrayal. Adult warm light-medium skin, naturally sized brown eyes, expressive strong eyebrows, slim long face, dark brown hair swept back into a LOW tied ponytail, small neat mustache/goatee. Navy Continental coat with broad buff lapels and cuffs, cream waistcoat, brass buttons, white ruffled stock/cravat, no epaulettes.
EXACT ACTING POSE, same in all 3 cells: three-quarter facing toward the viewer's RIGHT, speaking toward a partner to the right. An eager intellectual revolutionary pushing an idea forward: upper body inclined forward 8 degrees, shoulder line angled rather than horizontal, chin slightly forward, focused raised inner eyebrows and alert eyes. His near/visible arm is extended diagonally toward the right at chest level, elbow bent, hand in a precise rhetorical gesture with index and middle fingers loosely leading and palm turned a little upward; open confident hand, not pointing a threatening gun or casting a spell. The other arm is bent with hand touching or hovering by his sternum/coat lapel, fingers relaxed. Torso twist, arms and gaze form a clear diagonal toward the listener. In frame 3 only, the leading hand reaches a small step further to punctuate the point. Passion and urgency, a touch of youthful wit, not anger. Both hands empty.
